key_insight: Picard–Chebyshev weakly nonlinear analysis predicts how streak–planar-wave interactions generate oblique waves and harmonics that can trigger streak breakdown.
engineering_relevance: Predicting finite-amplitude transition triggers can inform disturbance-sensitive design and flow-control strategies for wall-bounded flows.
method: Formulate weakly nonlinear optimal perturbation analysis for compressible parallel flows using Picard–Chebyshev iteration.
Track non-modal amplification and nonlinear interactions across an expanding set of wave components.
Recover linear dynamics at first order and the weakly nonlinear amplitude equation at third order.
evidence_signal: For plane Poiseuille flow at Mach 0.3 and Reynolds number 3000, the abstract reports close agreement with DNS and identifies an optimal planar-wave perturbation that triggers streak breakdown in full nonlinear simulation.
watch_item: Accuracy is established here in the weakly nonlinear regime; broader operating conditions and computational costs as wave components proliferate require assessment.
paper_title: Predicting trigger in streak breakdown via Picard-Chebyshev approach in plane-Poiseuille flow
